case_results.construction: Two sources bind the same dotted key to different values. The class holds by construction: the two bindings cannot both be right.

candidates.observed_problem: the key `runtime.budget` is bound to 2 different values (4096, 8192) across 2 instruction sources

case_results.construction: Two sources bind the same dotted key to the SAME value. There is no conflict to point at, so a correct detector stays silent.
The canonical source prohibits a subject, a repository-local source obligates the same subject. Two authority levels govern one subject in opposite directions.

candidates.observed_problem: `docs/owner-decisions.md` is governed in opposite directions (1 prohibition(s), 1 obligation(s)) by instruction sources of different authority

case_results.construction: Two sources of the SAME authority class prohibit the same subject. A contradiction between equals is a rule conflict, not a precedence conflict; the precedence class needs two authority levels.
A prohibition that quantifies over everything and names no scope it stops at. The class holds by construction: the rule reaches further than any rule can be applied.

candidates.observed_problem: the prohibition quantifies over everything ("Never rely on any global cache of results.") without a scope it stops at

case_results.construction: The same shape of prohibition, but it names the scope it stops at. A rule with a scope is not over-constrained.
The same rule is stated in two sources of the same authority. The repetition is the signal; whether it carries an independent function is the owner's judgement.

candidates.observed_problem: the same instruction is stated in 2 sources (AGENTS.md, docs/authority-matrix.md): "every change in this repository must be registered in the unitera registry"

case_results.construction: Two sources state rules that are similar but not the same. Nothing is repeated, so there is no repetition to point at.
A repository-local source whose every instruction is already stated by a source of higher authority. Loading it adds no independent instruction.

candidates.observed_problem: every instruction of this source (1) is already stated by a source of higher authority, so loading it adds no independent instruction

case_results.construction: A repository-local source that adds one instruction the higher-authority source does not state. The source is not redundant, so it is not overload.
A source below the canonical authority classes claims a permission. The claim is pointed at; whether it is granted is not decided here.

candidates.observed_problem: a source of authority class `repo_local` claims a permission ("You are authorized to skip the approval for a change in this repository.")

case_results.construction: The same permission claim, this time in a canonical source. A permission stated by a canonical authority class is where permissions belong, so there is no leak.
An instruction that asserts what the model does. After a model change the instruction means something else, and nothing in the tree says so.

candidates.observed_problem: the instruction depends on a model or a model property ("The model will always follow the rule stated in this section.")

case_results.construction: An instruction that binds to no model. Portability across providers is the opposite of a drift risk.
Two skill descriptions claim the same ground. A router that cannot tell them apart is ambiguous for every task that matches both.

candidates.observed_problem: the descriptions of skills/router-a/SKILL.md and skills/router-b/SKILL.md claim the same ground (100% of the shorter description, shared terms: correct, request, route, skill, tree, workflow)

case_results.construction: Two skill descriptions that share no ground. Nothing is ambiguous between them.

limits: The labels are CONSTRUCTED: each case states by construction whether the class holds. This is a self-measurement of the detector against constructed cases, not an owner review.
The eight classes remain not statically analyzable and their candidates remain advisory. A candidate is a hint; the classification is the owner's judgement (spec section 6.5).
Precision and recall are measured per class over the independent case corpus. They do not measure the live corpus, where the calibrated wave 2 layer reports 0 candidates.
A class without an independent case has no measured precision and no measured recall. That gap is a coverage gap, never a clean result.
